messages:
alex: Heads-up: after landing the kernel-selection rewrite yesterday I see a new tail on small-batch decode (bs=2..4) — p95 went from ~18ms to ~30-40ms on several traces. Prefill paths look stable. Anyone started a bisect?

maria: saw some blips in the dashboard too, flagged a few requests with decode spikes. Noticed these correlate with seq_len around 64-96.

jon: interesting — did the selector change thresholding for flash vs paged? last patch made seq_len heuristics more aggressive for fused-flash.

alex: yeah the change tries to pick fused-flash-v2 for mid seq lengths, fallback to paged for >128. But spikes happen for short decodes after warmup. traces show kernel switch in-flight.

sam: can you paste a perf dump? also, do we see different KV-cache hit patterns for these requests?

alex: here's a short dump from a problematic run (trimmed):
```
[profile] request 0x7f3a: timeline:
  prefill: 12.2ms (flash-fused-v1)
  decode step 0: 3.8ms (fused-flash-v2 launch)
  decode step 1: 28.5ms (kernel switch + page-alloc)
  kvcache: page-scan=0->2, miss=1
  note: ctx_len 72, batch 3
```

maria: kernel switch + page-alloc looks suspect. Could be kernel launch overhead + smallpage alignment thrash. That 28ms is launch+mem work.

jon: do we have trace where the same request runs with fused-flash-v1 consistently? compare warm vs cold. Might be the selector oscillating due to transient seq_len rounding.

alex: I replayed one trace forcing fused-flash-v1 on decode path — tail disappears, p95 back to ~16ms. So selector logic is the variable.

perf-bot: auto-bisect started: comparing commit ab3f..cd4e for kernel-selection. Current suspects: heuristics that map seq_len->kernel and the paged fallback gating.

sam: quick mitigation: we could add a debounce on kernel switching inside a request (prevent switching after first decode step), or increase threshold for fused-flash-v2. Thoughts?

jon: debounce seems safe and small. Many decodes are continuous-batch streaming; if we prefer stability over micro gains it's fine. But need to check cost for very long sequences where fused-flash-v2 wins.

maria: propose: 1) quick revert to previous selector for canary hosts (low risk), 2) add unit test that simulates batch growth mid-request, 3) collect KV cache page-alignment metrics.

alex: agreed. Also add a perf counter for "kernel_switches_per_request". existing metrics only count launches globally.

sam: I ran a microbench forcing smallbatch decode with KV fragmentation. Results (median of 50 runs):
```
bs=3, seq=72:
  fused-flash-v1: median 17.1ms, p95 19.8ms
  fused-flash-v2: median 15.3ms, p95 34.6ms (high tail)
  paged-attn: median 20.0ms, p95 22.2ms
notes: v2 has lower median but unstable tail when kv pages allocate mid-decode.
```

jon: that matches the hypothesis. v2 optimizes kernel codepaths but is sensitive to memory pathing and smallpage rework.

perf-bot: repro artifacts uploaded to /runs/2171112222-repro. Check run 7 for log + nvprof snapshot.

maria: action items:
- alex: add kernel_switches_per_request metric + increment on any switch
- sam: add debounce (skip switching if decode_step > 0 and current_kernel != chosen_kernel) behind flag
- jon: instrument KV allocator to log page-fragment events for requests that hit p95
- ops: rollback selector on canary hosts until flag-tested

alex: I'll open a small PR for the metric and the canary. sam if debounce reduces p95 we can promote.

sam: prototype done locally. With debounce enabled (flag=decode_debounce=1) microbench p95 for v2 drops to 18.2ms, median stays ~15ms. Sending draft PR shortly.

jon: good. Also check continuous batching codepath: if we stop switching mid-request, need to ensure we don't starve future batches. Maybe allow switch only at prefill boundaries or on explicit reset.

alex: noted. We'll gate the debounce to only apply when request_continuous_batching==true. That avoids harming prefill policy.

maria: leaving a note: potential long-term fix is to make kernel choice depend on kvcache_page_alignment + live mem pressure, not just seq_len. But that's more invasive.

alex: for immediate triage I'll: deploy canary rollback, enable decode_debounce on canary, push metric. If all green we'll roll to prod and follow up with page-aware selector.

sam: thanks — I'll attach perf graphs once PR lands. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: canary rollback completed on 3 hosts at 2025-11-03T16:12:10Z. Monitoring p95...

alex: closing loop — initial canary shows p95 back to ~18ms, no regression at 30min. Keeping thread open for 24h.

jon: small note for release notes: "avoid in-request kernel switches for decode streams; add kernel_switches_per_request metric"

maria: adding to release notes draft and infra alerts.

alex: thanks all. Follow-ups: postmortem if any regression persists.
